method: Independent clean-room source audit of all runtime modules and runtime tests, generated official protocol types and response schemas used at runtime boundaries, gateway transport/dispatch/receipt cross-checks, and native UID launcher lifecycle inspection. Existing archival source/tests/history and personal homes were not read. Findings were reproduced using a fresh isolated NativePort substitute, then a separate official 0.164.0 process exercised immediate terminal disconnect cleanup without model turns.

findings.title: History reports completeness without checking the native item-loading contract
reproduction: Return an official-shaped turn with items:[], itemsView:notLoaded and nextCursor:null from thread/turns/list.
The result contains complete:true while its turn explicitly declares itemsView:notLoaded.
findings.impact: Unloaded or summary payloads can receive the full-history readiness claim. The native request asks for full items but the received evidence is not validated before publishing.

findings.title: Incomplete history does not prevent backend turn admission
reproduction: Read a first history page returning a non-null nextCursor and complete:false.
Submit turn/start from the same client without reading the remaining pages.
The runtime issues turn/start once; admission checks activity but no complete history proof.
findings.impact: The HIST-02 invariant depends entirely on browser state and does not hold at the final runtime write boundary.

findings.title: Definitively rejected turns permanently pin unused attachments
reproduction: Upload one attachment and submit it on an idle thread.
Let the native turn/start return native_error with delivery:not_sent after its write boundary.
Try attachment/remove: it returns attachment_in_use; index.json retains the thread pin despite no accepted turn.
findings.impact: Known unused data remains undeletable and consumes the fixed attachment quota across restart. A rollback must preserve earlier accepted/unknown references and concurrent reference ownership.

findings.title: Disconnected history contexts retain all traversal capacity
reproduction: For 256 client identities, complete an empty paginated history and call clientDisconnected.
Read the same thread from a new client.
History fails with capacity/History traversal capacity exhausted although every prior client has disconnected.
findings.impact: The declared 256-context bound becomes a lifetime limit, requiring worker restart for later users. Late reads must also be fenced so cleanup cannot be undone.

findings.title: Read-classified thread resume accepts configuration mutations
reproduction: Call thread/resume without an operation ID and include options.sandbox or options.approvalPolicy.
Dispatcher treats it as a read, bypassing mutation receipts and maintenance admission.
Runtime forwards the configuration overrides through official ThreadResumeParams.
findings.impact: A recovery/read endpoint can modify model and permission configuration without the declared mutation boundary. This is established from the public contract and dispatch source, not a commercial provider test.

findings.title: A known first-turn rejection is also published as unknown live activity
reproduction: Create a native thread successfully, then definitively reject its first turn with delivery:not_sent.
The composite outcome correctly retains the partial thread identity, but runtime also sets that thread activity.unknown=true.
The thread is placed in activeThreads even without a turn ID. Reads cannot clear it, and the gateway's busy check blocks its restart recovery route.
findings.impact: Partial creation facts and current live-work uncertainty are conflated; the known idle partial thread can unnecessarily disable new work and browser recovery. Gateway restart admission is being reviewed separately.

additionalObservations: The official MCP elicitation response schema requires only action; validatePrompt currently rejects omitted content for decline/cancel and url acceptance even though native optional/null fields are part of PROTO-02. This was identified during final schema review and needs a focused legal-default regression.
Opaque attachment IDs being reusable across administrator tabs is explicitly documented, so it was not reported as an authorization bug.
Stopped-journal recovery exists in deployment code, so the persisted activity barrier was not incorrectly reported as having no reset path.

checks.coverage: Four isolated deterministic boundary reproductions; not a repair regression or native integration.
Eight official 0.164.0 Windows PTY open/immediate-disconnect cycles returned terminal count to zero with no error events; native PID exited during cleanup. No model turn was issued.

limitations: This is a pre-audit with actionable findings; it is not one of the three formal clean rounds and does not authorize a full suite.
No real provider inference, account login, external MCP, personal CODEX_HOME, retired 110 host, or 192.168.1.120 operation was performed.
Linux UID, sudo, subreaper, cgroup, directory-mode and process-tree behavior was inspected statically only; the Windows native terminal check does not establish those platform guarantees.
No actual 0.149.0 history migration was performed; the legacy branch's structure is not native backward-compatibility evidence.
Gateway, web and HTTPS source was concurrently being repaired by other reviewers. Cross-boundary line references describe the inspected pre-repair state and must be rechecked on the final snapshot.

The entire generated protocol inventory was not manually read; the official bundles, runtime-used contracts and all runtime method adapters were examined. Unused generated API types are outside this focused pre-audit.
